chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes sexually impure (junub), then sleeps until morning. Can he fast that day voluntarily? He said: Is he not free to choose between himself and midday?
He said, And I asked him about the man who has a wet dream during the day in the month of Ramadan. He completes his fast as he is. He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does a wet dream or overnight sexual impurity break the fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility of fasting validity based on the timing of ritual purification (ghusl) rather than the moment of impurity. It establishes that for voluntary fasting, the window to purify and fast extends until midday, while for Ramadan, a daytime wet dream does not invalidate the fast, reflecting the Shia principle that impurity itself does not break the fast unless accompanied by eating or drinking. This ruling underscores the distinction between the conditions of the obligatory Ramadan fast and general voluntary fasting in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man comes to be with sexual impurity, then he sleeps until the morning. Can he Fast that day voluntarily?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is he not with the choice what is between him and what is between half the day?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who bed wets during the day in the Month of Ramazan, he complete his Fast just as he is.’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences sexual relation (because of which Ghusl (bath) is obligatory); then goes to sleep until the morning, if he can fast that day an optional fast. He (the Imam) said, ‘Up till midday it is up to his choosing.’
I then asked about a man who experiences wet dream during the day in the month of Ramadan; if he completes his fast as it is. He (the Imam) said, ‘It (completing) is not harmful.’”
